title: Three in-tree NF4 quantizers, and they disagree on nibble order (trueno packs high-first, aprender-gpu and aprender-train low-first)
evidence: measured 2026-09-27 (la-72) on la-72/0.72-shaping @cab19f8502: crates/aprender-gpu/src/kernels/quantize/nf4_cpu.rs:151 packs idx_lo | (idx_hi << 4) (first element low); crates/aprender-train/src/train/transformer_trainer/wgpu_nf4.rs:189-192 packs the even element low; crates/aprender-compute/src/brick/quant_ops/nf4.rs:186 packs (high << 4) | low with the first element high (doc :120). All use 64-element absmax blocks and the NF4 LUT. Bytes packed by one path and unpacked by another swap every pair of weights. Spike S-R4c used the aprender-gpu one, because the CUDA QLoRA path trains on it.
ask: Pick one canonical NF4 packer (the CUDA training path's aprender-gpu kernels::quantize_nf4 is the one R4/QQE-005 depend on). Make the other two call it or delete them (fold = move), and add a cross-implementation byte-equality falsifier.
owner: cop to assign (0.72 R4 owner, or R14)

title: lora/qlora.rs QLoRALayer quantizes the base with symmetric int4 (quant4bit, -7..7), not NF4
evidence: measured 2026-09-27 (la-72): crates/aprender-train/src/lora/qlora.rs:53,71 call quantize_4bit; crates/aprender-train/src/quant/quant4bit.rs:10,71,153 is q = round(clamp(x/scale,-7,7)) with scale = absmax/7, which is symmetric uniform int4 with 15 levels, not the NF4 normal-quantile LUT. Anything calling the CPU QLoRALayer 'QLoRA' is therefore not the QLoRA the CUDA path (NF4) trains, and the two cannot be compared at 1e-2 (S-R4c: Q4_K-vs-NF4 base gap is rel .33-1.20 per tensor).
ask: Either switch QLoRALayer to the canonical NF4 quantizer (see la72-nf4-three-quantizers), or rename it to Int4LoRALayer and make every doc and CLI path that says NF4/QLoRA name the scheme it actually uses. Add a falsifier asserting the quantizer's level set.
